text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000589 bills 99215 far above expectation, mostly on low-complexity patients, yet the few returned charts document high MDM, so the conflict is unresolved.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern points toward upcoding: most 99215s fall on patients with zero or one chronic condition, and the sampled low-complexity 99215s are often routine presentations such as upper respiratory infection (C0308231, C0308237) or low back pain (C0308234, C0308336), with no high-complexity 99215s in the sample. Against that, all six documented 99215 claims, including C0308238 and C0308383, were recorded at high MDM, and no documented claim at any level fell below the billed code. That would normally favor a legitimately complex panel, but six charts out of 51 99215 claims is too thin to settle the question. Three notes claim moderate-or-higher data reviewed with no lab or test line on the claim, which is weak evidence that some documentation may be templated or inflated rather than reflecting the visit. A reviewer should first pull charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215s, especially the URI and back-pain visits, and compare the high-MDM notes for cloned language. They should also check whether the documented data review matches orders or results actually on file."}
